subject: Request: 3-week MAP extension & contingency plan (ACME)
messages:
From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2027-12-12T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP timeline check-in

Hi Olga,

Quick heads-up from procurement: our legal review for the data residency addendum has slipped and we now expect sign-off no earlier than Jan 5. That pushes our expected go-live by ~3 weeks.

We want to be transparent — ACME is committed to Redwood, but this affects our internal deployment calendar (security onboarding and SRE runbook testing). Can you advise what you need from our side to update the MAP and any impact on the committed pricing/credits?

Appreciate your help,

—Laura Jensen
VP, Platform Partnerships
ACME Corp

(Attachment: procurement-redline-summary.pdf)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-12T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP timeline check-in

Laura — thanks for flagging and for the transparency. I'm sorry to hear the legal review slipped; totally understand how those cycles can push dates.

High-level response and asks:
- We can accommodate a 3-week extension to the MAP milestone dates.
- To update the MAP cleanly I need: the latest redline (legal), the expected sign-off date, and any SSO/KMS scheduling constraints.
- Operational impact: a 3-week shift keeps the current dedicated capacity allocation but will move the canary plan out by 2 cycles; that may change our cutover window and SRE test dates.
- Commercial impact: Marcus will confirm whether a short credit or pro-rated invoice adjustment is appropriate given the delay.

I've attached a draft MAP v3 with the proposed date shifts and a first-pass risk ledger (ACME_risk_log_20271212.csv). Please review and confirm the sign-off target; if Jan 5 holds we'll update the MAP and circulate a formal mutual action plan amendment.

Next steps:
1) Laura / procurement to confirm final sign-off date and provide the legal redlines (if any).
2) ACME to confirm any new blackout windows for SSO/KMS (Tim?).
3) Marcus to confirm commercial position on credits / invoice adjustments.

I'll queue this for a brief internal triage and loop Jonas if we need exec-level approval.

Best,

Olga Petrov
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx; ACME_risk_log_20271212.csv)

From: jonas.weber@redwood.com <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.jensen@acme.com
Date: 2027-12-13T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP timeline check-in — escalation for credit approval

Olga — quick read and guidance:
Thanks for the draft and the clear asks. I'm ok with a short MAP amendment to shift milestones by 3 weeks. From an executive perspective we should offer a small operational credit for the missed canary window — keeps goodwill and preserves the go-live momentum.

Marcus: please advise on an appropriate credit (suggested range 5–10% pro-rata for the delayed service period). If the contract requires a formal change order, start the DocuSign draft and include the new MAP dates.

Olga: once Marcus confirms the commercial, push the revised MAP and the risk ledger to ACME and ask for confirmation of Jan 5 (or updated date). If ACME requests SOC2 evidence, provide the high-level summary and point to the secure drive link — do not send raw artifacts over email.

Jonas Weber
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com, tim.harris@acme.com
Date: 2027-12-14T10:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP timeline check-in

Thanks, Olga and Jonas — that approach sounds reasonable. Procurement confirms Jan 5 as a target for legal sign-off, though Tim noted there is an internal policy review that could add a day or two.

We would appreciate the operational credit while we finalize. Also please include a short SOC2 evidence summary and a link to your secure folder; procurement will not accept the full binder by email.

I'll review ACME's latest redlines and send them by EOD tomorrow.

—Laura

(Please see: procurement-redline-summary.pdf — will follow with full redline doc.)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.com <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Laura Jensen <laura.jensen@acme.com>
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-12-20T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Final: MAP amendment + risk journal attached

Laura, team — attaching the formal MAP v3 and the updated risk journal after incorporating the procurement redlines. Highlights:
- All milestone dates shifted by 21 days; canary & SRE windows moved to Feb 6–10 (new target).
- Commercial: Marcus approved a 7% pro-rata operational credit applied to the first month post-go-live. We will include a line in the DocuSign amendment.
- Risks captured: legal sign-off slippage, SSO provisioning delay, test-run capacity contention. Each risk has owner and mitigation steps in the ledger.

Attachments: ACME_MAP_v3.xlsx, ACME_risk_log_20271212.csv, SOC2-evidence-summary.pdf

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/13421/ACME-2026-0421), secure drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1aB2c3D-ACME-MAP)

Please confirm acceptance of the MAP amendment so Marcus can route DocuSign. If ACME needs anything faster, ping me and we'll set up a 30-min sync.

Thanks — Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
(Attachment stubs included above)
